chapter.title: Chapter Seven: Return of the Block
chapter.subtitle: The list belongs to everyone.
chapter.description: Restore the open bracket and make Blue answer for changing it.

tips: Use SQUABBLE before the encounter ends.

starObjectives.description: Use SQUABBLE before the encounter ends.

preDialogue.speaker: Promoter
preDialogue.text: Everybody stop where you are. Nobody plays, nobody packs up, nobody goes to the car. I need thirty seconds and I need you to hear them once.

preDialogue.speaker: Promoter
preDialogue.text: Last night, after closing, somebody took the original entry sheet off this bar and crossed a name off it. One name. Somebody's got a recording of when it happened. I'm not going to say who,

preDialogue.speaker: Promoter
preDialogue.text: because I want to see if anybody volunteers.

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: *(Low, to you.)* Champ, don't go up there yet.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
preDialogue.text: I have both copies and the original's missing. Promoter, I want it on the record that I'm not accusing anybody. I want it on the record that a list went out with thirty-one names on it and came

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
preDialogue.text: back with thirty.

preDialogue.speaker: Promoter
preDialogue.text: Thirty-one should be thirty-one.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
preDialogue.text: It's thirty.

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: Because you's got a newcomer. You're on that sheet. You've been on that sheet since you walked in here.

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: *(Not looking at Blue.)* It's thirty.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: One line. It was one line, and I was going to put it back.

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: When.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: After.

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: After he got turned away. After he stood at that gate and somebody told him he wasn't on the list. You were going to put it back *after*.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: I said what I said.

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: You didn't say anything. That's the problem. You've been doing this for four years and you never say the whole thing.

preDialogue.speaker: Promoter
preDialogue.text: I'm going to say this once and then I'm going to stop talking and let the match schedule go. Every name on that sheet — every single one — is provisional until I know which one was crossed and

preDialogue.speaker: Promoter
preDialogue.text: why. That includes people who like each other. It especially includes people who like each other.

preDialogue.speaker: Promoter
preDialogue.text: That means you're not playing until this is settled. I know that's not what you signed up for. I'm not going to pretend I can make it right by giving you a good table.

preDialogue.speaker: Snitch
preDialogue.text: *(To nobody in particular, raising the phone slightly.)* So, the footage is—

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
preDialogue.text: Snitch.

preDialogue.speaker: Snitch
preDialogue.text: I'm just saying it *exists*—

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
preDialogue.text: You said I'd ask first. I'm asking now. Not here.

preDialogue.speaker: Snitch
preDialogue.text: *(Puts the phone down.)* Fine. But it's going to come out either way, and I'd rather it came out with my thumbprints on it than with a caption somebody else wrote.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
preDialogue.text: *(To the room, then to you.)* Red checks the footage. Cornball checks the bar. I need one person who was here all night and wasn't on camera.

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: They were on camera.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
preDialogue.text: On a phone somebody else was holding, at the far end, with the mic pointed at the gate. I need somebody who was actually *looking*.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
preDialogue.text: *(He waits, and he doesn't put it to the whole room. He puts it to you.)* Where were you at closing?

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
postDialogue.text: Say it in front of them.

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: *(To the room.)*I was at the corner table. Blue came in after the last game. He took the sheet off the bar, he was standing right there, and he uncapped his pen before he walked away. I watched

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: him do it. Nobody was filming it.

postDialogue.speaker: Cornball
postDialogue.text: What else.

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: He didn't go straight out. He stood by the bar and he read the whole sheet. He put his thumb on it twice.

postDialogue.speaker: Wifey
postDialogue.text: Twice where.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* I was deciding whether to do it at all.

postDialogue.speaker: Wifey
postDialogue.text: That's not where you put your thumb.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: I know where I put my thumb, Wifey.

postDialogue.speaker: Wifey
postDialogue.text: Then say it out loud, because he can't, and you just did it for him.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: *(Long beat. He doesn't look at the player.)* There was a second line. Under his. I got that far and I stopped.

postDialogue.speaker: Cornball
postDialogue.text: The second line is them.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: It's a scratch.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
postDialogue.text: Blue.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: It's *scratched*, Red, and it came off, and it isn't the same as a pen.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
postDialogue.text: It's the same pen.

postDialogue.speaker: Snitch
postDialogue.text: *(Quietly, to his phone, not to anyone.)* I got the whole minute. If he put the pen down twice, it's in there. I can pull the frame.

postDialogue.speaker: Wifey
postDialogue.text: You know what's funny? You've been running this block for four years. You know everybody's name. You wrote half of them yourself.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: Wifey—

postDialogue.speaker: Wifey
postDialogue.text: You didn't hesitate on his. Everybody's watching you not hesitate on his. And then you got to mine, and you stopped, and you want me to notice the *good* part.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: *(It comes out fast.)*I know how it looks. I *know* how it looks. My brother walks in after four years and everybody's lining up to take a picture, and I'm the one who's been holding this thing

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: together, and everybody acts like I got here yesterday because he was on a poster. Four years. I kept it going. I kept it going with *myself* and nobody in this street ever once asked me what that

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: cost.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
postDialogue.text: That's not what I asked you.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: I know it's not.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: *(Beat. Much quieter.)*I'm not asking you to make it smaller. I did the line under his name. I'll say it in front of everybody and I'll say why. But I'm not going to stand here and be told I'm

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: nothing but the one who did it, because you're all ready for that and it would be so easy, and I have been *so* ready for it.

postDialogue.speaker: Promoter
postDialogue.text: *(He hasn't raised his voice once.)*That's enough. Both of you, I don't want your history, I want the list. *(He turns to you.)*You. You said you watched him take it. That makes you a witness,

postDialogue.speaker: Promoter
postDialogue.text: which means you're also the last person in this street whose account nobody else can check. So here's what I'm asking. I don't want you to protect him and I don't want you to bury him, and I'm not

postDialogue.speaker: Promoter
postDialogue.text: going to tell you which one you look like right now.

postDialogue.speaker: Promoter
postDialogue.text: Is your name crossed out or isn't it.

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: It was a scratch. But I was on that line, and if I say it was a scratch, then next time somebody puts a pen to a sheet on this block, I don't get to be the one who was standing here looking at it.

postDialogue.speaker: Wifey
postDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* No. You don't.

postDialogue.speaker: Snitch
postDialogue.text: *(Already unmuting himself.)* Okay so, for the record, that is a hell of a thing to say out loud on a—

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
postDialogue.text: Snitch.

postDialogue.speaker: Snitch
postDialogue.text: I'm *saying it's good*. I'm saying it's good. Let me have the good thing.

postDialogue.speaker: Promoter
postDialogue.text: Then here's where we are. Cracked Head's name goes back on the list — he earned it, I never took it from him, somebody else did, that's not in dispute. Blue's out of the title bracket. That was

postDialogue.speaker: Promoter
postDialogue.text: the rule before he broke it and it stays the rule after.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: Fine.

postDialogue.speaker: Promoter
postDialogue.text: And the thirty-first name — *(he looks at you)*— stays on the sheet, in ink, with a line through it, initialed by me, dated today, in a drawer, because I don't know whose hand did it and neither

postDialogue.speaker: Promoter
postDialogue.text: do you. It stays there. If anybody in this street ever touches a list again, that sheet comes out and we all look at it.

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: Including mine.

postDialogue.speaker: Promoter
postDialogue.text: *Especially* yours. That's the last thing I have that isn't a rumor.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
postDialogue.text: *(To the player, not unkind, which is worse.)*You know what you just did. You didn't say you saw him take it. You didn't get him put back on. You just made sure nobody could quietly do that again,

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
postDialogue.text: including yourself, and now you're gonna have to be the person who says that out loud every time somebody on this block wants a list changed.

postDialogue.speaker: Wifey
postDialogue.text: That's a job.

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: I know.

postDialogue.speaker: Wifey
postDialogue.text: It's not a title. You don't get to put it on a shirt. It doesn't come with the crown. It comes with being the person everybody's a little afraid of, forever, and nobody's ever gonna thank you for

postDialogue.speaker: Wifey
postDialogue.text: it.

postDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
postDialogue.text: Whoever's been holding the sheet all night — the original.

postDialogue.speaker: Promoter
postDialogue.text: I don't have it.

postDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
postDialogue.text: Yeah. *(He looks at Blue.)* You do.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* It's in my jacket.

postDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
postDialogue.text: I'm not asking you for it. I'm asking you in front of everybody, so that when it turns up later, nobody can say I came in here and took something off you.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: *(Throws it. It lands on the bar.)* There. It's the whole sheet. Thirty-one. Count them.

postDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
postDialogue.text: *(He doesn't pick it up.)* I don't want it.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: It's *yours*, Cracked.

postDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
postDialogue.text: I know whose sheet it is. I don't want to be handed a thing by you in front of a crowd. *(Beat.)*You want to give it back, you read it out. Right now. All of it, including whatever's under my

postDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
postDialogue.text: name, and I'll stand here while you do it.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: He doesn't start.

postDialogue.speaker: Snitch
postDialogue.text: *(Almost gently.)*Champ. There's a roof over on Red's side. Nobody's on it. *(Beat.)*His brother's on it, but he's sat down. You can go up or you can stay down. Both of those are fine and only one

postDialogue.speaker: Snitch
postDialogue.text: of them is useful.

starObjectives.description: Use SQUABBLE before the encounter ends.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
preDialogue.text: Show me.

preDialogue.speaker: Snitch
preDialogue.text: I know.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
preDialogue.text: Full minute. No soundtrack. No crop.

preDialogue.speaker: Snitch
preDialogue.text: Red, I *know*, we've had this conversation—

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
preDialogue.text: Then show me.

preDialogue.speaker: Snitch
preDialogue.text: I can't. Not yet.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
preDialogue.text: Why not.

preDialogue.speaker: Snitch
preDialogue.text: Because I told a room in chapter four that I was going to ask first, and a man who says he'll ask first and doesn't ask is a *specific kind of liar*, and I've spent a long enough life being a

preDialogue.speaker: Snitch
preDialogue.text: different kind of liar that I don't want to find out which one I am under pressure.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
preDialogue.text: Who are you asking.

preDialogue.speaker: Snitch
preDialogue.text: Blue. I've asked Blue. He said go ahead, he said he wanted it out, and I want to be very clear that Blue telling me to post it is not permission, because the man who wants you to say it is not the

preDialogue.speaker: Snitch
preDialogue.text: man it happens to.

preDialogue.speaker: Snitch
preDialogue.text: So. Cracked Head. I've got to ask him in person, and I can't do it over a phone, and I can't do it on a stream, and I can't do it in a room with a camera in it.

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: *(From the door.)* Then you go where he is.

preDialogue.speaker: Snitch
preDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* Yeah.

preDialogue.speaker: Snitch
preDialogue.text: *(To the player.)* Come with me. Not because you're muscle. Because if he asks why I'm shooting this, I need somebody standing there who can say I asked in a room with no camera in it.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: Fine.

preDialogue.speaker: Snitch
preDialogue.text: *(To Red, quieter.)* If he says no, I'm posting it anyway. I want that said now, out loud, in front of a witness, so that when I do it I can't pretend I was confused later.

preDialogue.speaker: Snitch
preDialogue.text: *(To the player, walking.)*He beat me the first night and I've been carrying it around like a grudge, which is embarrassing, because I lost fair and square and I've made my whole living off not

preDialogue.speaker: Snitch
preDialogue.text: understanding losses.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: You're asking a man who threw a punch at his own family if you can film it.

preDialogue.speaker: Snitch
preDialogue.text: I'm asking a man if I can film a man who threw a punch at his own family. *(Beat.)*See, those sound the same out loud. They're not the same on paper. But I gotta say it out loud, because it *is*

preDialogue.speaker: Snitch
preDialogue.text: the same, and the difference is just what I write in the caption.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: What are you gonna write.

preDialogue.speaker: Snitch
preDialogue.text: *(Walking.)* "I asked." Two words. That's the whole caption.

preDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
preDialogue.text: I know why you're here. Red told me. He told me about nine minutes ago and then he told me I couldn't leave the spot, so I've been standing here being told I can't leave the spot.

preDialogue.speaker: Snitch
preDialogue.text: Cracked Head, I'm going to publish a minute of video of your brother taking an entry sheet off a bar and crossing your name off it, and I came to ask you first, in a room with no camera, in

preDialogue.speaker: Snitch
preDialogue.text: daylight.

preDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
preDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* That's a real question.

preDialogue.speaker: Snitch
preDialogue.text: It's a real question.

preDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
preDialogue.text: Ask Red.

preDialogue.speaker: Snitch
preDialogue.text: I did. Red sent me to you.

preDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
preDialogue.text: *(Almost smiling.)* Then Red knew the answer.

preDialogue.speaker: Snitch
preDialogue.text: I can't use that. That's you being gracious and I need it to be you *deciding*.

preDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
preDialogue.text: Post it.

preDialogue.speaker: Snitch
preDialogue.text: You want to think about—

preDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
preDialogue.text: I've been on a list and off a list in a week, and one of those was done to me by my brother and one of those was done to me by *him*, in front of a bar, while I stood here. *(Beat.)*I want

preDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
preDialogue.text: everybody to see the minute. I want it to be the whole minute, including the part where he stops and puts the pen down, because that part's the only reason I'm asking you to do it.

preDialogue.speaker: Snitch
preDialogue.text: *(Carefully.)* There is no part where he puts the pen down.

preDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
preDialogue.text: There's a part where he *doesn't*. Same thing. *(He looks at the player.)* You're the one who was standing there.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: He stopped.

preDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
preDialogue.text: He stopped.

preDialogue.speaker: Snitch
preDialogue.text: *(Writing on the soft piece of paper.)* I asked. He said post it. It's in a room with no camera and there's a witness whose job is not to lie to me.

preDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
preDialogue.text: *(To the player.)* That job. They gave you a job.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: They didn't give it to me. I picked it up.

preDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
preDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* Worse.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
postDialogue.text: Full minute. Nothing cut. Play it loud enough that the people at the back can hear the *before* and the *after*, because the before is the part they've heard and the after is the part they

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
postDialogue.text: haven't.

postDialogue.speaker: Snitch
postDialogue.text: Full minute. *(He plays it.)*

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
postDialogue.text: Say what everybody's thinking.

postDialogue.speaker: Snitch
postDialogue.text: There's two names on that sheet who weren't on it when he picked it up. There's thirty-one and there's thirty.

postDialogue.speaker: Wifey
postDialogue.text: There's thirty.

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: I wasn't on the original sheet. Wifey, look at the second line.

postDialogue.speaker: Wifey
postDialogue.text: *(Not moving.)* I'm looking at it.

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: You don't have to read it out. But you have to look at it in front of Promoter, and he's standing right there, and if you look at it here first then Promoter can't say somebody fed him a story.

postDialogue.speaker: Wifey
postDialogue.text: *(Very flat.)* He was on the second line.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: Wifey.

postDialogue.speaker: Wifey
postDialogue.text: I know what it says. I wrote it. I have the original in the office and I wrote the second line myself at nine in the morning and I remember doing it.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: Then stop.

postDialogue.speaker: Wifey
postDialogue.text: *(Not stopping.)* No. That's the fourth time tonight somebody's told me to stop holding a piece of paper and I've had a *season* of it.

postDialogue.speaker: Snitch
postDialogue.text: *(Low.)* She's got it. I'm not touching it.

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: Promoter's going to ask who else looked and what they saw. The answer's going to be three people who all saw a different thing, and the block's going to spend a week picking which one to believe.

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: So somebody has to hand him the list, and the names, and say *all of them, and here's who they were.*

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: Including me?

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: Especially you. You don't get to be the one who held the pen. You get to be the one who said it out loud, in order, with the count.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* Okay.

tips: Use SQUABBLE before the encounter ends.

starObjectives.description: Use SQUABBLE before the encounter ends.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: Play me. No stakes, no stamp, nothing on the line. I want a match where I can lose and there isn't a *reason* for it.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: That's a bad reason to want something.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: It's the only honest one I've had all week.

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: Blue. Before you start. *(She's got a clipboard she's not reading from.)* I want to say one thing and I want to say it in front of them, and then I don't want to talk about it again tonight.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: Wifey—

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: I let you come home and tell me it was not our business. I helped Baby Momma plan a memorial. I knew what you did and I let you do it, and I said in the back room at Auntie's that I picked the

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: version where I got to keep my life, and that was true, and I've been *correct* about it for a month, and I want somebody else to have heard me say it who wasn't in the room.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: I heard you.

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* Thank you. I know what that's worth. I know it's not a lot.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: It's not about what it's worth. It's about how many people you have to say it to before you believe it.

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: *(Loud.)* BLUE. Blue, I got a question about a thing and it's not about your brother.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: Cornball, I swear to God—

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: It's a *procedure* question and it's going to come up anyway, so we can do it now while there's still a person in here who'll say no.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: What.

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: Four years ago you gave somebody a location, and you didn't do it because you were angry that day. You did it because you were angry *every* day, and one of them was the day it mattered. And I

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: want to know which one this is.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: It's not the same.

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: That's not a no.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: It's not a *yes* either.

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: Blue, I ran a clipboard for you tonight for nothing. I got you an hour of tables and I never charged anybody a dollar and you know why I do it, and I do it because I think you're a man who shows

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: up. And I watched you hold that pen over a page for a count of four, and that was the same hand. That was the *same hand*, and you stood here an hour ago and told a room you learned something, and

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: I need you to tell me whether you actually learned it, because I am going to be standing behind a table in five minutes either way and I'd like to know what I'm working for.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: I don't know.

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: That's the first thing you've said tonight that I believe.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: *(Beat.)*If I'd been in my right mind I would have crossed both of them. I want that on the record before I say the next part, because the next part is the part that's going to sound like an

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: excuse, and it isn't one. I was standing at that bar and I was so tired of being the brother that everybody forgives first. My brother walks in and the whole street wants to give him something.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: Nobody's ever offered me anything. So I picked up a pen to make it *even* for about four seconds, and then I thought about what my father would have to say, and I put it in my pocket.

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* And?

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: And that's the part that's gonna sound bad. I put it in my pocket because I was *scared of him*, not because I was brave.

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: Okay. *(He writes it down.)*I'm writing that down, because in about nine minutes you got up there and read thirty-one names, and I want it on paper that I asked you what you learned and you told

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: me *I don't know*, and that's the *truth*, and if you change it up there I'm going to be the one who says so.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: Cornball—

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: Don't make me the guy who let you. I've got a clipboard and a good eye and I been right once tonight, and I am *not* doing it again for free.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: You're baiting me.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: Yeah.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: You put it on the middle three times and I've been over it three times and you *let* me.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: I'm trying to see if I know when I'm doing it.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: Do you?

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: *(Beat.)*Yes. I knew all three times and I let you take them anyway, because I didn't want a good game, I wanted to be *beatable*, and that's — *(He stops.)*That's a different thing to admit out

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: loud than I thought it was going to be.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: It's a bad thing to admit out loud.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: It's the first *true* thing I've said in a month. You're gonna have to get used to it.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: Good game. I was about to tell you the shuffle was bad.

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: It was fine.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: I know. I'm trying to stop before the sentence comes out. *(Beat.)* Take the list to your brother. You know which sentence belongs there.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: I've got the sentence.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: *(To Wifey, not to the player.)* He's the one who says it?

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: He's the one who means it.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: *(Not to the player. To the table.)*It's a *list*. I kept thinking about it like it was a *list*. Thirty-one names on a piece of paper, and I picked up a pen, and I thought I was fixing a

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: *roster*.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: My brother came home after four years. He doesn't have a house. He doesn't have a *job*. He's got a bag and a *key* he still thinks works, and this whole street decided he was a gift. And the

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: thing I was actually doing up there at that bar was I was trying to make sure *somebody* had to look at *him* instead of me for five minutes.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: That's it. That's all of it. I didn't hate him. If I'd hated him I would have had a reason and I could have lived with it.

postDialogue.speaker: Cornball
postDialogue.text: *(Writing.)*I'm not looking at you. I'm writing it down. Those are two different things and I need you to know the difference, because if I look at you right now I'm gonna say something and I

postDialogue.speaker: Cornball
postDialogue.text: promised I'd save it for in front of everybody.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* That's fair.

starObjectives.description: Use SQUABBLE before the encounter ends.

preDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
preDialogue.text: Promoter called. My entry's back.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: He said you'd say it in front of them.

preDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
preDialogue.text: *(To the player.)*He said I'd say it in front of *you*. Which is a different thing, and I'm not going to be the man who complains about the difference, because you're the only person on this list

preDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
preDialogue.text: who hasn't asked me for anything.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: *(Coming over, and stopping, and the stop is the whole scene.)* Cracked.

preDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
preDialogue.text: Blue.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: I'm not going to say a version of this that makes me sound like I've been carrying it. I wasn't. I decided on Sunday and I did it Sunday and I didn't think about it for four days, which is —

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: *(He stops, because he can hear how that sounds.)*— which is worse. A man who thinks about it for four years and does it anyway has a *reason*. I did it in four seconds.

preDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
preDialogue.text: You didn't even decide. That's what I'm going to think about at three in the morning. It wasn't a decision. It was a *gesture*.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: Yeah.

preDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
preDialogue.text: And you can't take it back by being honest about it, and I need you to hear that I know that, and I'm not going to punish you for the honesty either, because I'm *tired*, Blue. I have been angry

preDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
preDialogue.text: for six days and it turns out six days is nothing. Four years is nothing. I'm going to be angry about this until I'm forty and it's going to be a *thing I do*, and it isn't going to be a *story*

preDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
preDialogue.text: that has a shape.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: I'm not going to be able to make this right. I want to say that now, before I go up there and say a lot of other things, because I don't want you hearing the speech and thinking one of the

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: sentences was the real one. There isn't a real one. There's just a list of things I could've done and I did the other thing.

preDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
preDialogue.text: You can still be my brother.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* I'm not sure that's yours to give.

preDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
preDialogue.text: No. It isn't. *(Beat.)* But I can't be the one who cuts you off either, or I'm just doing the same thing you did with a *nicer* reason, and I'd rather be angry. So. We clear.

preDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
preDialogue.text: You know what the worst part is?

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: Tell me.

preDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
preDialogue.text: He's not wrong. *(Beat.)*That's the worst part. I've been up here for a week telling people he did it out of jealousy and a bad heart, and I'm standing in a gate and he says *I didn't hate him*

preDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
preDialogue.text: and it's — *(He stops.)*You can't build a whole four years of *resentment* on somebody who's just *tired*. I had to have somebody be the villain. I needed one of you to be the villain so the other

preDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
preDialogue.text: one could be forgiven, and now I'm gonna have to do this without that.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: That's a bad place to be standing.

preDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
preDialogue.text: It's a *terrible* place to be standing. I have got a final tomorrow and I have to be a *person* on Saturday and I don't have the *thing* I was going to use.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: Then don't use it.

preDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
preDialogue.text: What?

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: You can play the final tomorrow and *still* be angry with him. I know that sounds like a joke because he's going to hear it like a joke, and it's not, and here's the actual thinking: you've been

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: holding your whole argument in one person. If you let him be a coward, you never have to find out whether you'd have forgiven him anyway. *(Beat.)*That's not a reason to hate him. That's a reason

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: to hate *yourself* and you'd rather not, and neither would I, so I think you play the final and you stay angry and you let those two things be in the same room.

preDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
preDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* You've been here eight weeks.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: Nine.

preDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
preDialogue.text: Nine weeks. *(Beat.)*I'm gonna win tomorrow, and when I do, I'm going to be a *bad* champion, and I'm going to be bad at it *specifically* because a stranger told me to hold two things at once.

preDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
preDialogue.text: You understand that you're making this worse on purpose.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: Yeah.

preDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
preDialogue.text: *(And he laughs — one, short, surprised out of him.)* Okay. Yeah. *(Beat.)* Don't get comfortable being right.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: That one's mine now.

postDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
postDialogue.text: You got me again. Different play this time.

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: Different play because you changed your opening. I could see it coming.

postDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
postDialogue.text: I *know* you could see it coming. That's why I did it. I wanted somebody to see me try a thing.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: From a distance, and he doesn't come over.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: You leaned too hard on the middle.

postDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
postDialogue.text: *(Without turning.)* I did.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: You always do when you're mad.

postDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
postDialogue.text: You haven't said a word to me in a week and that's the first coaching thing you've said since we were kids.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: I've been banned from my own tables. I don't get to do it right.

postDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
postDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* You could come up here.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: Not today.

postDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
postDialogue.text: Not today. *(Beat.)* Okay. Not today works.

preDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
preDialogue.text: Side match, if you've got time. I'm hiding from people asking whether we're "back together."

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: I can make a sign.

preDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
preDialogue.text: I would rather you tell Snitch to stop putting question marks over pictures of us.

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: He has a whole *folder* of those. He has a folder for *each* of you and he has *named* them, and one of them is just the word "denial" in a font I don't like.

preDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
preDialogue.text: What is he doing with these?

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: He's making a *timeline*. *(Beat.)*Ma'am, that man is building a *documentary* and nobody is *hiring* him and he is doing it anyway, out of *love*, which is the *worst* possible fuel for a

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: documentary.

preDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
preDialogue.text: They asked me at the grill table. Whether you and I were "working on it." Like it's a *work order*.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: What'd you say?

preDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
preDialogue.text: I said "no." And then one of them said "so when's the *rest* of it," and I had to walk away from a *grill*, champ, so you can see how today is going.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: You could've said something worse.

preDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
preDialogue.text: I had nine or ten things loaded up and I didn't use *one* of them, because I'm not performing for a *grill*. *(Beat.)*Sit down. Ten minutes with somebody who knows how to mind their own business.

preDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
preDialogue.text: *(To Cornball.)*Not you.

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: I know how to mind my own business. I mind it *professionally*. I mind it so well they gave me a clipboard.

preDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
preDialogue.text: *(Sitting down hard, like the match let go of something.)* He asked me what our child likes for breakfast.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: That's ordinary.

preDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
preDialogue.text: It's the first *ordinary* question anybody's asked me since he got back. Four weeks. Four weeks of "how do you *feel*," "what did they *say* to you," "did he say *anything*," and I have been

preDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
preDialogue.text: *cracked open* in a *courtyard* by three separate people who wanted to be *in the story*.

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: That's 'cause that's the good part and nobody wants the good part. The good part don't have a *clip*.

preDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
preDialogue.text: It doesn't have a clip because it's a *Tuesday*.

preDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
preDialogue.text: Pancakes. That's the answer. No syrup on 'em, little cup on the side, because he's four and he thinks syrup is a *thing you add later* and not a thing that goes *on*, and I've been telling him

preDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
preDialogue.text: that for three years and I have never once said it to the man, and I said it to *him* in about four seconds because he *asked*.

preDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
preDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* I don't know what that means yet. I'm not going to tell him what it means. I'm going to see if he *remembers* it.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: And if he remembers?

preDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
preDialogue.text: Then I'll know he's been paying attention to the wrong thing for four years and I don't know yet if that's better or worse. *(Beat.)*Ask me on Sunday. It's a week. People can be a week from

preDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
preDialogue.text: knowing things.

postDialogue.speaker: Cornball
postDialogue.text: *(Not to anybody.)* You know, I been holding a clipboard all day and everybody's had the biggest *day* of their *life* on it and the most anybody wrote down was a *thing about chairs*.

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: That's a job.

postDialogue.speaker: Cornball
postDialogue.text: It's a *thing* with a clipboard. *(Beat.)* I got a question and it's a real one and it's not about the day, so don't get that look.

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: Cornball.

postDialogue.speaker: Cornball
postDialogue.text: Saturday. When this all finishes. You said you were gonna hold the line. You said it ain't a title and it don't go on a shirt. And I been watching you all day and I've seen what it *costs* — it

postDialogue.speaker: Cornball
postDialogue.text: costs you *everything you were gonna say next*, and then you just *don't say it*, and I watched you do that *four times* in six hours and you didn't even *notice*.

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: I noticed.

postDialogue.speaker: Cornball
postDialogue.text: *(Beat.)*Okay. Good. I just needed to know if it was costing you or if you were just *good at it*, because if you're just good at it, then this block has got a problem, and if it's costing you

postDialogue.speaker: Cornball
postDialogue.text: then this block has got a *different* problem, and I gotta know which one I'm writing down on Saturday.

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: Write down the second one.

postDialogue.speaker: Cornball
postDialogue.text: *(Finally writing.)*The second one. *(Beat.)*That's a *horrible* thing to have on a clipboard and I'm gonna do it anyway, and if anybody asks me, I'm a *setup volunteer* and I have *no opinions*

postDialogue.speaker: Cornball
postDialogue.text: about any of this.

tips: Use SQUABBLE before the encounter ends.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: *(Knocking.)* You in there?

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: I'm auditing.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: It's a list of names.

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: It's *thirty-one names and a question*, and if I'm going to hand this to Promoter I am going to hand him a *document*, because I have watched two men in this family destroy themselves with a

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: *piece of paper* and a *feeling*, and I am not doing that again with a *third* one.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: You're doing it right now.

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: *(Not looking up.)* I know.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: Checking is a way of not asking.

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: *(Beat.)*I know that too. *(She sets the bottle opener down.)*I have been *counting* since four o'clock, champ, and the counting is not the *work*, and I have been *telling* myself the counting is

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: the work since four o'clock, and I would like to be *able to stop counting*, and I have been *trying to stop counting* for about six weeks.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: What's on the list, Wifey.

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: Two names missing. His. And — *(Beat.)*And the second line. Your name, at nine in the morning, in my handwriting, with a *line* through it. And a note in the margin in his hand that says

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: *(she reads it out flatly)*"check with W before this one."

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: He wrote you a note.

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: He wrote *himself* a note. That's what that is. He didn't know which one to do, so he *wrote himself a note* and put it in his *jacket* and left.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: Promoter's going to want to know about that note.

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: I know.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: And if it comes out, it's going to look like I was part of it. Somebody who helped write a list that had my name on it.

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: *(Quietly.)* Yes.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: You could've burned it.

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: I thought about it for about nine seconds. *(Beat.)*You know what stopped me? I thought about the version of me where I *did* that, and I heard the voice, and it was my *husband's* voice, and it

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: was *grateful*. And I'd rather be *scared* than grateful, and I have never once in four years had that thought, so.

preDialogue.speaker: Promoter
preDialogue.text: I've had it since this morning. It's in a drawer with a date on it and both of you' names on the outside, so nobody has to wonder who went looking for what.

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: You kept it.

preDialogue.speaker: Promoter
preDialogue.text: I kept it because I'm the only person here who isn't related to anybody. *(Beat.)*It means nothing, it means the second line got scratched, and it's going in a drawer either way, and I'd rather it

preDialogue.speaker: Promoter
preDialogue.text: be in a drawer with a date than in a rumor.

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: Here. Take it. I've been holding it since four o'clock and I want it out of my hands before nine.

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: The list's in the drawer. Promoter's got it. Cracked Head's on it, you're on it, and there is a *note in the margin in his own handwriting* that I am going to be thinking about for the rest of my

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: life.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: "Check with W before this one."

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: *(Beat.)*In *fairness* to him, I would've told him no. If he'd *asked* me. Which he didn't, because he knew. *(Beat.)*Which is the part. He didn't ask me because he already knew what I'd say, and

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: he wrote that down so that later he could tell himself it was *pending*.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: Does that make it better or worse?

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: *(Getting up.)*It makes it *exactly* the same and it takes a *year* off my life. Come on. Play me. I need thirty minutes of a thing where I can *lose* on purpose, because the alternative is I sit

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: in that office until nine and I become a *person who audits*.

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: *(Flat, and not remotely upset.)*There. I lost. That was deliberate and I want credit for it in a *written record*, because I am going to need to prove to myself in about a week that I am capable

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: of losing on purpose.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: You needed it.

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: I have been *winning* at everything for four years and it turns out that's *also* a way of not asking anybody anything.

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: *(Getting her coat.)* Blue. The final sheet's ready for your announcement.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: You coming up there with me?

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: I'll be where you can see me. *(Beat.)*You're doing the talking, Blue. And I'm going to be *right there*, and that's not me *supporting* you, that's me making sure you *say the number out loud*,

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: because if you say "a couple names" I will correct you in front of the whole block and I won't do it gently.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: Wifey—

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: *Thirty-one.* And one line. Say it that way.

postDialogue.speaker: Cornball
postDialogue.text: *(To nobody, doing the work.)* Thirty-one. And I wrote 'em all down while he was talking, and the one he got stuck on, I wrote it slower, so I'd remember I wrote it.

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: Which one did he get stuck on?

postDialogue.speaker: Cornball
postDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* Not telling you that. That's the *one* thing on this clipboard that's actually mine.

starObjectives.description: Use SQUABBLE before the encounter ends.

preDialogue.speaker: Promoter
preDialogue.text: Thirty seconds. What you changed, whose name is back on, and what it costs you. That's it. Any more and I'm stopping you.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: I crossed Cracked Head off the entry list. He qualified. I took him off.

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: ...There it is.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: I'm going to read the list. All of it. Because I know what "a few names" sounds like, and it's the thing I've been doing for four years, and I'm not doing it tonight.

preDialogue.speaker: Promoter
preDialogue.text: It'll take a minute.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: It'll take a minute.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: *(Reading.)* …Wifey. *(Beat.)* Red. *(Beat.)* Cornball. *(Beat.)* And — *(and here it is)* — *[the player's name]*.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: I want to say something about that name, and I want to say it right, and I want to say it before I read the last ten, because it's going to get easier in a minute and I don't want to be the man

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: who did this at the part where it was easy.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: There's a second line. It was scratched. I put the pen on it. *(Beat.)*I wrote myself a note in the margin that says "check with W before this one," and I put that note in my jacket, and I left,

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: and I have been telling myself for eight hours that that was *deciding* to leave it alone. It wasn't. I already knew what Wifey would say. I wrote the note so that later I could call it *pending*.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: And I want to say the other thing, which is that if that scratch had been a name I cared about, I wouldn't have put the pen down at all. The reason I stopped is that I couldn't do two of them in

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: one night. *(Beat.)*That's not restraint. That's *scarcity*. I want it in the record that I didn't stop because I was good. I stopped because I ran out.

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: I heard him.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: Cracked Head's entry is restored. He earned it. Mine is out of the title bracket. That was the rule before I broke it and it's the rule now.

preDialogue.speaker: Promoter
preDialogue.text: Championship list is final. *(He holds up the paper.)* Thirty-one. One line, scratched, initialed, dated, in a drawer. Nobody's got to guess after tonight.

preDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
preDialogue.text: Thank you for saying it yourself.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: You don't have to thank me.

preDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
preDialogue.text: I know. Don't make me regret it.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: I'm not done, and I know I'm done, so I'm going to say one more thing and then I am going to stop for the rest of my life.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: Four years ago I gave somebody an address, and I did it because I was tired of being the brother that everybody forgives first, and I have spent tonight telling y'all I learned something. I

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: didn't. *(Beat.)*I *remembered* something. There's a difference and I only worked out what it was about an hour ago, and it's this: knowing what you did is not the same as being a different man. I

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: have known what I did for four years. It didn't make me a different man. It just made me *quiet*, and I spent the quiet building tables.

postDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
postDialogue.text: Blue. *(Beat.)* For what it's worth — I don't want you to be somebody else. I tried that, for a year. You're *easier* to be around as the guy you are.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: That's a hell of a review.

postDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
postDialogue.text: It's a *hustle*, not a review.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: Champ. One thing.

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: Say it.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: If I get up there and I do the *thing* — the voice, the bit about how much I did for this block — do you stop me.

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: No.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: Why not?

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: Because it might be true, and because if I stop you from saying a true thing to make you look better, that's me deciding what you're allowed to feel about your own block.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* That's a hell of a job you got.

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: It's not a job. It's a Tuesday.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: *(Almost smiles.)* Don't make it a *thing*.

postDialogue.speaker: Cornball
postDialogue.text: Thirty-one.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: *Thirty-one.*

postDialogue.speaker: Cornball
postDialogue.text: And you're not gonna say "a couple."

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: I'm not gonna say "a couple."

postDialogue.speaker: Cornball
postDialogue.text: Good. I'll be right here with the rest of 'em, in case you start.

preDialogue.speaker: Promoter
preDialogue.text: Last one today. You two are still in for tomorrow and this changes nothing, so the two of you can stop playing like it's the third.

preDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
preDialogue.text: One last look at your deck before the real thing, champ.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: I'll keep score.

preDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
preDialogue.text: No. *(Beat.)* Red can keep score. You can sit down here if you want.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* All right.

preDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
preDialogue.text: *(Waiting.)* You're doing the thing where you look at your deck for nine minutes.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: I'm doing the thing where I know you're about to open the same way.

preDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
preDialogue.text: And?

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: And I'm not going to stop you, because I want to see what you do when somebody doesn't stop you.

preDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
preDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* You keep doing that. The thing where you let me find out something on my own.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: It's cheaper than telling you.

preDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
preDialogue.text: Good game. I'm saving something for tomorrow.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: You said that after the last one.

preDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
preDialogue.text: And I meant it after the last one.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* What did you save?

preDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
preDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* I'm not gonna tell you tonight.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: Okay.

preDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
preDialogue.text: That was easy.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: Yeah. *(Beat.)* It's what I do now.

preDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
preDialogue.text: *(From the wall, dry.)* There. Almost a normal conversation. Try to not get ambitious with it.

preDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
preDialogue.text: I had a whole thing planned and she took it in one sentence.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: She does that.

preDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
preDialogue.text: I've been doing it for four years. You're just *arriving late*.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: Cracked.

postDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
postDialogue.text: Mm.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: Can I ask you a thing and have you not make it a thing.

postDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
postDialogue.text: You can ask.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: Did you ever get a letter. From the lawyers, or the — did anybody ever write you a *paper* thing, and I never knew, because I would have *taken* it. I would have carried it around. I would have

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: handed it to Wifey and she'd have put it in a *drawer* and I'd have never asked what was in the drawer.

postDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
postDialogue.text: No.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: Nothing?

postDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
postDialogue.text: *(Beat.)*I sent a message once, through Red, that said *I know*. That's it. Four words. I wanted somebody to have written me something, because I was somebody people *wrote* to, and then I wasn't,

postDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
postDialogue.text: and there's no *mail* about that. *(Beat.)*You want to know the funny part?

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: What.

postDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
postDialogue.text: I drafted that message forty times. And every version said *I miss you*, and every version I deleted, because *I miss you* is a thing you say to somebody who's *coming back*, and I was not sure I

postDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
postDialogue.text: was ever doing that. So the one I sent said *I know*, and it was the only true thing in it, and I have been sorry about it for four years.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: For what it's worth, I would've come to the door.

postDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
postDialogue.text: I know.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: Any of them. All of them. I was *right there*.

postDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
postDialogue.text: I know. *(Beat.)* That's the whole problem, and it's also the only good news, and I've been carrying both of them since Tuesday and I need to go sit down.

scenes.speaker: Delivery Demon
scenes.text: Package for whoever handles the rooftop. Owner's notice. *(He doesn't come in. He puts it on the table and steps back.)* Buyer visit is tomorrow afternoon.

scenes.speaker: Promoter
scenes.text: Buyer? He told me in *March* we had the roof for the final.

scenes.speaker: Delivery Demon
scenes.text: You do. The booking's clean. That ain't a notice about the booking, that's a notice about the *building*.

scenes.speaker: Cracked Head
scenes.text: He used to threaten to sell every time the rent was late. He did it twice. He never *meant* it and he got the *water* running every time.

scenes.speaker: Promoter
scenes.text: There's a name on it. Techbro Rich. I'll ring the owner in the morning.

scenes.speaker: Ganger Blue
scenes.text: So we finally got the whole *thing* running — the open entry, the schedule, the *list* — and now somebody wants to buy the *floor*?

scenes.speaker: Baby Momma
scenes.text: First find out what's happening. Then panic. In that order would be brand new for us.

scenes.speaker: Cornball
scenes.text: *(Writing, and he's writing a *number*.)* Twenty-two years I've been on this block. I want somebody to tell me what it *was*, so I can write it down, because in about nine months there ain't gonna

scenes.speaker: Cornball
scenes.text: be a *here* to write it down about.

scenes.speaker: Promoter
scenes.text: Cornball, we don't know if it's selling—

scenes.speaker: Cornball
scenes.text: I don't care what's selling. I care what's *gone*. *(Beat.)*That's different. A thing can be sold and still be *here*. A thing can be sold and everybody come back and it's a *building*. It ain't

scenes.speaker: Cornball
scenes.text: about the roof. It ain't about the *floor*. It's about whether there's a *place* where the *list* means something, because that's the only part of any of this that was ever *ours*.

scenes.speaker: Player
scenes.text: What do you need.

scenes.speaker: Cornball
scenes.text: *(Beat.)*Somebody's gotta find out what the *rules* are gonna be. The man buys a *roof*, the roof don't come with *rules*, so somebody's gotta go ask for 'em, and the somebody has to be a person

scenes.speaker: Cornball
scenes.text: who can go in there and be *asked* not to be nice about it.

scenes.speaker: Wifey
scenes.text: That's you.

scenes.speaker: Player
scenes.text: *(Beat.)* I know.

scenes.speaker: Wifey
scenes.text: *(And she doesn't say "don't." That's new, and everybody notices.)* Then take the morning. I'll cover the circuit.

scenes.speaker: Delivery Demon
scenes.text: *(Heading out.)* For the record — the owner told me to say it's not a warning. He said, and I want you all to hear that he said it, "tell them it's not like the rent."

scenes.speaker: Ganger Blue
scenes.text: *(To nobody in particular, to the bar, to the room.)* It *is* like the rent.
